title: Alan Turing's Life In Reverse, From Bletchley to London #Shorts
description:
Alan Turing's life is told backwards in this episode, opening at his death in Wilmslow in 1954 and rewinding through the years after the war to his birth in west London in 1912. The journey steps through Manchester's first computers, the design of the stored program machine at Teddington, the naval codebreaking at Bletchley Park, and the 1936 paper that described the machine now named for him. Every scene moves to an earlier year, so the machines and the ideas appear in reverse order and the costs of his conviction become clear. Dates and places follow the documented record, and the accounts that dispute his death are named as disputed.

Made with AI assistance.

scenes.narration: He broke the German naval codes that helped win the war, and the state then punished him for who he loved.
Step backwards and Alan Turing is running the machines that execute the first programs and writing the manual that teaches others how.
Earlier his paper on what a machine can decide describes the computer before any computer existed, in 1936.
Before that he rides a bicycle to a country house in 1939 and starts reading the naval ciphers no one could break.
At the start there is a boy sent to a classics school who keeps his science and a friend whose death in 1930 he never forgot.
